title: Holographic Representations of Topological Quantum Criticality: Emergent Symmetry Approach around the Bott Clock
abstract: In this article, we apply the idea of emergent symmetries to construct holographic representations of a broad class of topological quantum critical points (tQCPs) that appear in fermionic classes in the Bott clock. We show explicitly that around the Bott clock, an emergent symmetry $U_{EM}$ exists at a tQCP between different symmetry protected gapped phases with protecting symmetry $G_p$ in $d$ spatial dimensions. This emergent symmetry can be used to construct a $(d+1)$ spatial dimensional lattice model with a properly upgraded symmetry such as $U_{EM}\times G_p$ or $U_{EM} \rtimes G_p$, etc. By doubling the degrees of freedom of the adjacent topological class in $d$-dimensions, we successfully show that the $(d+1)$-dimensional lattice models constructed in this way have the desired enlarged symmetry groups that precisely belong to the adjacent topological classes, counterclockwise around the Bott clock. Furthermore, $d$-dimensional boundaries of these $(d+1)$ dimensional lattice models of gapped topological classes are shown to exhibit identical infrared dynamics as the corresponding tQCPs in the $d$-dimensional adjacent topological phases in the Bott clock, with lower symmetries.
summary: This work develops a holographic framework to describe topological quantum critical points (tQCPs) using emergent symmetries. By relating the gapless physics at a tQCP in $d$ dimensions to the boundary states of a gapped topological superconductor in $d+1$ dimensions, the authors establish a systematic method for classifying and understanding these critical points across different symmetry classes.
main_problem: The paper aims to construct holographic representations for a broad class of topological quantum critical points (tQCPs) by employing the concept of emergent symmetries.
main_result: It demonstrates that the tQCPs can be mapped to the boundary states of higher-dimensional gapped topological superconductors, establishing a systematic holographic relationship around the Bott clock structure.
method: The core method involves using an emergent symmetry ($U_{EM}$) at the $d$-dimensional tQCP to construct an enlarged symmetry ($	ilde{G}_p$) for a $(d+1)$-dimensional bulk model, whose boundary dynamics then match the tQCP's infrared physics.
model_or_system: The study focuses on fermionic topological states, specifically within the framework of the Bott clock structure, involving Symmetry Protected Topological (SPT) phases in various dimensions ($d$ and $d+1$).
key_observables: Emergent symmetries ($U_{EM}$), protecting symmetries ($G_p$), and the infrared dynamics of the boundary states.
important_parameters: The spatial dimensions ($d$ and $d+1$) and the specific symmetry groups involved in the topological classification.
main_assumptions: The approach assumes that the anomalous degrees of freedom at the tQCP can be matched to the gapless surface fermions of a higher-dimensional bulk theory.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the four-step holographic construction procedure, mapping IR EFTs to UV lattice models. Figure 2 compares the structure of $d$-dimensional SPTs to $(d+1)$-dimensional SPTs, showing the holographic link.
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops the holographic construction, starting from the identification of emergent symmetries at tQCPs, upgrading the symmetry to define a higher-dimensional bulk model, and finally proving the boundary correspondence.
why_interesting: The holographic mapping between lower-dimensional critical points and higher-dimensional gapped phases provides a powerful theoretical tool for understanding quantum criticality in strongly correlated systems, linking symmetry protection across dimensions.
